title_en: The Signs of the Hour, Part One
body_ar:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين وأصلي وأسلم على من بعث رحمة للعالمين وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين.

أما بعد فإن الله سبحانه وتعالى قد أخبرنا أن الساعة آتية لا ريب فيها، وقد بين أن هذه الأمة آخر الأمم، فهي ختام الأمم فلن تقوم الساعة إلا على بقاياها، والساعة حدث عظيم، يقتضي من هذه الأمة التهيؤ لأن تكون ختام هذه الدنيا، وأن تستعد لأن تكون فاتحة الآخرة فنحن الآخرون السابقون كما قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، هذه الأمة تختم بها الدنيا فهي آخر أممها وتفتتح بها الساعة فهي أول أممها، أول الأمم تدعى بين يدي الله هذه الأمة،
body_en:
In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Ever-Merciful. All praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds, and I ask God to bless and grant peace to the one who was sent as a mercy to all the worlds, and to his family, his Companions, and all who follow his guidance and keep to his sunnah until the Day of Judgement.

To proceed: God, glorified and exalted, has told us that the Hour is coming, in which there is no doubt, and He has made clear that this community (ummah) is the last of the communities. It is the seal of the communities, and the Hour will not come except upon those left of it. The Hour is a momentous event, and it requires of this community that it make itself ready to be the close of this world, and that it prepare itself to be the opening of the next. For we are the last to come, the foremost, as the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said. With this community this world is sealed, so it is the world's last community; and with it the Hour is opened, so it is the Hour's first community. The first of the communities to be summoned before God is this community,

flags.context: فنحن الآخرون السابقون كما قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
options: we are the last to come, the foremost
we are the last [of the communities in time], the first [on the Day of Resurrection]
we are the latecomers who go first
flags.note: A quotation of the hadith نحن الآخرون السابقون يوم القيامة. The Sheikh quotes it without the concluding words, so the two poles of the contrast (last in time, first on the Day of Resurrection) are left implicit in the Arabic. Option 1 makes them explicit but supplies wording he did not give. A reviewer should set the house practice for truncated hadith quotations.

translator_notes: The published page carries only the opening excerpt of this lecture/sermon; the Arabic breaks off mid-sentence and the full text is offered on the site as a downloadable Word document. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends. Nothing has been supplied to complete it.
الساعة is rendered 'the Hour' throughout, the standard English for the eschatological term.
